note: Literature establishes that FDXR variants cause a wide phenotypic spectrum ranging from optic atrophy/auditory neuropathy to severe infantile-onset encephalopathy and mitochondriopathy, supporting residual activity genotype-phenotype correlations.

evidence.text: Biallelic mutations in the FDXR gene cause mitochondrial disease, peripheral neuropathy, and optic atrophy with variable severity of phenotypes and neurodegeneration.

source.title: Biallelic mutations in FDXR cause neurodegeneration associated with inflammation
source.quote: Recently, we have identified biallelic mutations in the mitochondrial flavoprotein "ferredoxin reductase" (FDXR) gene as a novel cause of mitochondriopathy, peripheral neuropathy, and optic atrophy. In this report, we expand upon those results by describing two new cases of disease-causing FDXR variants in patients with variable severity of phenotypes

evidence.text: Biallelic missense variants in FDXR cause autosomal recessive auditory neuropathy, optic atrophy, and early-onset severe retinal dystrophy, highlighting the spectrum of sensory oculopathy and genotype-phenotype correlations.

source.title: FDXR-Associated Oculopathy: Congenital Amaurosis and Early-Onset Severe Retinal Dystrophy as Common Presenting Features in a Chinese Population
source.quote: Biallelic pathogenic or likely pathogenic FDXR variants were identified in 11 unrelated patients, including 14 missense variants of which 10 were novel.

numbers.metric: unrelated patients with biallelic FDXR variants
